content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Explain the properties of metals in terms of structure and bonding
Describe and explain the properties of alloys
is the type of bonding found in metals and alloys. It involves a unique structure where electrons are shared across all the atoms, giving metals their characteristic properties.
Metal atoms lose their outer electrons
Positive metal ions are arranged in a regular lattice
Ions are held together by attraction to the delocalised electrons

because they flow around the positive ions like a sea.
Delocalised electrons can move and carry charge
Strong metallic bonds throughout the structure
Layers of ions can slide over each other without breaking bonds
Can be drawn into wires - layers slide
When a voltage is applied, electrons flow in one direction
This flow of electrons is an
[DIAGRAM: Electrons moving through metal when voltage applied]
Delocalised electrons gain energy when heated
They move faster and collide with other electrons and ions
Energy is transferred quickly through the metal
Metals are malleable (can be hammered into shape) and ductile (can be drawn into wires) because:
The delocalised electrons move with the ions
The structure doesn't break - it just changes shape
[DIAGRAM: Layers of metal ions sliding while maintaining bonding]
In ionic compounds, if layers shift, like charges end up next to each other and repel - the structure shatters. This doesn't happen in metals.
Why Different Metals Have Different Melting Points
Stronger metallic bonding, higher melting point
Ions closer together, stronger attraction, higher melting point
Magnesium and aluminium have higher melting points than sodium because more electrons are delocalised, creating stronger metallic bonding.
are mixtures of two or more metals, or a metal mixed with a non-metal (like carbon).
Different sized atoms are mixed into the metal structure
This disrupts the regular arrangement of atoms
[DIAGRAM: Comparison of pure metal structure vs alloy structure]
Can be designed for specific properties
Why Alloys Are Harder Than Pure Metals
Pure metals have layers of same-sized atoms that can slide easily.
Different sized atoms disrupt the regular layers
Layers cannot slide over each other as easily
This makes the alloy harder and stronger
Saying metals conduct because they have "free electrons"
Thinking metallic bonding is weak because metals can be bent
Metallic bonds are strong; metals bend because layers slide while maintaining bonding
Alloys are mixtures of metals, not chemically bonded compounds
Describe the structure of a metal. (3 marks)
Explain why metals are good conductors of electricity. (3 marks)
Explain why copper can be drawn into wires. (3 marks)
Magnesium has a higher melting point than sodium. Explain why. (3 marks)
Explain why alloys are harder than pure metals. (3 marks)
Steel is an alloy of iron and carbon. Explain why steel is used for construction rather than pure iron. (3 marks)
